nodes.label: NASA SVS Record 3912 — Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature
nodes.author: Greg Shirah, NASA/GSPC
nodes.norm_label: nasa svs record 3912 — global sea surface currents and temperature

nodes.label: ECCO2 Global Currents + SST Still (2048x1024)
nodes.author: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio / Greg Shirah

nodes.label: Surface Current Filament / Particle-Trace Field
nodes.rationale: Ocean flow is drawn as dense white-line particle streaks rather than vector arrows or a raster heat map, because the flowing texture is what makes current direction and shear legible at a glance in a still frame.

nodes.label: ECCO2 High Resolution Ocean and Sea Ice Model (MITgcm)
nodes.norm_label: ecco2 high resolution ocean and sea ice model (mitgcm)

nodes.label: Flat Equirectangular Global Map Render
nodes.rationale: A single flat (equirectangular) world frame rather than an interactive globe: the project is a static, prerendered page, so a wrapped 2D projection at 2:1 aspect (2048x1024) gives a simple background plate that scales to any viewport without a WebGL sphere.

nodes.label: Dark Gray Continent / Bathymetry Backdrop
nodes.rationale: Land is rendered as a desaturated dark gray plate (GTOPO30-derived) rather than satellite imagery, so the colored ocean remains the only saturated element and the continents read as negative space.

nodes.label: Sea Surface Temperature Color Encoding
nodes.rationale: Current speed is encoded as line density and temperature as hue (dark blue -> cyan -> green -> yellow -> orange -> red), so one channel carries motion and the other carries heat without a separate legend image.

nodes.label: Single Animation Frame (19 Jun 2007 12:00Z)
nodes.rationale: Only one decoded frame is shipped instead of the source animation: it keeps the page's payload at a single ~1 MB JPEG and avoids any live or video dependency, at the cost of freezing a 2007 state that must be labelled as 'not a live view'.

nodes.label: ECCO2 / ECCO Cube92 Legacy Product
nodes.rationale: A model-observation synthesis on a cube-sphere grid at 18-30 km with 50 vertical levels, fitted to observations by least squares; it is not a direct measurement at every grid point, and its native cube-sphere grid is not a simple latitude-longitude image a browser can treat as one.

nodes.label: NASA SVS Record 3912 (verified fields)
nodes.rationale: Verified directly from the page API so the interface can cite title, release, credits, datasets, and 2007-03-25 to 2008-03-03 coverage without inventing anything.

nodes.label: ECCO V4r4 Is Not a Substitute for the Render's Source
nodes.norm_label: ecco v4r4 is not a substitute for the render's source
nodes.rationale: Downloading V4r4 (1992-2018, >3 TB, ~90 products on 0.5 degree and llc90 grids) and treating it as 'the data behind the image' would be a provenance error, so the project does not do this.
nodes.source_location: 6 Current ECCO distribution is not a substitute

nodes.label: Licensing and Attribution (NASA public domain, ECCO citation, OFL, ISC)
nodes.norm_label: licensing and attribution (nasa public domain, ecco citation, ofl, isc)
nodes.rationale: NASA SVS content is public domain unless noted and only one rendered still is used, but media guidelines still imply no endorsement, so the project credits the publisher and scientists and states it is not an official NASA product.

nodes.label: Audio Boundary (SonificationEngine interfaces)
nodes.rationale: A mapping is an inspectable scientific claim; physical ranges live on the scientific variable rather than the audio mapping; the scene owns time, not the UI; AudioContext is created only after a user gesture, and AUDIO_STATUS encodes the honest current state.

nodes.label: DataStatus Type
nodes.rationale: Availability is independent of provenance: a dataset can be scientifically real and still be not-connected, which is exactly the ECCO2 state.

nodes.label: NASA SVS API Client (server-only, unused)
nodes.rationale: Exists so a future acquisition job has one controlled entry point instead of ad-hoc fetches in components; `import "server-only"` prevents client bundling, and it is not called in Stage 1 so the demo does not depend on a government server at runtime.

nodes.label: Normalization Functions (normalizeLinear / normalizeLog)
nodes.rationale: Returns null for non-finite input, zero-width ranges, non-positive log values, and invalid ranges; null means 'no audio value' and must not be replaced with zero because zero is a real data value. Deliberately free of dataset-specific constants.

nodes.label: NormalizedSample Contract
nodes.rationale: A normalized sample retains the original sourceValue so the audio value can always be traced back to the data value.

nodes.label: ProvenanceLayer Type
nodes.rationale: Four layers (scientific-data, rendered-visualization, derived, synthetic) are never merged, so derived data cannot silently become 'raw'.

nodes.label: ScientificVariable Contract
nodes.rationale: Units are explicit with `unknown` rather than guessing, and validRange must name its source.

nodes.label: Sonification Transport Component
nodes.rationale: The entire transport is offline in Stage 1: play, speed, and layer controls are disabled and visible copy names the missing engine and numerical fields instead of simulating activity.

nodes.label: Visualization Plate Component
nodes.rationale: A strict 2:1 rectangle with four 9px cyan corner ticks and the only shadow in the product; loading and error states never lose the caption or source credit so provenance survives failure.

nodes.label: Explore Route (/)
nodes.rationale: Renders title block, plate, disabled transport, then rail so evidence is read after the image but before any control; VisualizationPlate is the only client component because it tracks image load state.

nodes.label: Open Question: Exact 2012 ECCO2 Release
nodes.rationale: The SVS record names ECCO2 and MITgcm but not the run identifier, build date, forcing set, or checksums; because the render was released in 2012 it likely used an older run than the currently listed Cube92, but that is an inference recorded as a question, not asserted in the interface.

nodes.label: Bundled Still Is Frame 25000 (19 June 2007)
nodes.rationale: NASA's frame-timestamp file maps frame 25000 to 2007-06-19T12:00:00Z, so the still is one instant rather than a temporal composite; the distinction is surfaced in the plate caption. The API filename's '2028x1024' is treated as a publisher typo because measured pixels and structured metadata say 2048 x 1024.
nodes.source_location: 4 The bundled still is a single frame

nodes.label: Stage 2 Extension Points (5 steps)
nodes.rationale: Ordered path: acquire a defensible subset, convert to a browser contract, normalize and map, implement the Web Audio engine, then add equivalent non-audio state. validRange must come from dataset metadata, never from a rendered image.

nodes.label: Numerical ECCO2 Access Blockers
nodes.rationale: No anonymous numerical endpoint was verified, PO.DAAC requires Earthdata authentication (credentials must never reach the browser), the current product is terabytes across hundreds of thousands of granules, the 2012 release is unnamed, and the cube-sphere grid does not map to an image.

nodes.label: Verification Method (three accepted proofs)
nodes.rationale: A source counts as verified only if its publisher returned the record over HTTPS, its file was downloaded and measured, or its metadata was read from a machine-readable API; snippets, reposts, memory, inferred values, and color-picked pixels are rejected as evidence.

nodes.label: Stage 1 Scope (visual foundation only)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately ends at the verified metadata plus one rendered still: no numerical ECCO2 fields, no sonification engine, and no claim that pixel colors are measurements, because faking a subsystem would violate the product's honesty principle.

nodes.label: Stage 1 Status Table (available vs not available)
nodes.norm_label: stage 1 status table (available vs not available)
nodes.rationale: The transport is deliberately disabled so the interface explains the missing subsystem rather than simulating it; NASA's visualization is a rendering, not a measurement.

nodes.label: Rule: Never Sample Rendered Pixels as Measurements
nodes.norm_label: rule: never sample rendered pixels as measurements
nodes.rationale: The plate is a rendered visualization, not numerical data; sampling pixel colors would convert a rendering choice into invented measurements and imply data the project does not have.

nodes.label: Rule: Color Picking Is Not Data Extraction
nodes.norm_label: rule: color picking is not data extraction
nodes.rationale: Compositing and antialiasing alter color and no validated per-pixel legend exists, so pixel sampling would convert a rendering choice into invented data; the colorbar variant was therefore not bundled or transcribed.
nodes.source_location: 5 What the image can and cannot support / 11 Rules for future data work

nodes.label: Eight Rules for Future Data Work
nodes.norm_label: eight rules for future data work
nodes.rationale: Never infer a measurement from a rendered image, keep provenance labels distinct, name the release, measure the asset (bytes/checksum/query/date), keep credentials server-side, state any release mismatch in the interface, use null rather than zero for missing samples, and label synthetic fixtures in the UI.

nodes.label: Three Distinct Layers (scientific / rendered / derived)
nodes.rationale: The layers must not be collapsed into a single 'NASA data' label; otherwise a customer-facing claim would conflate a model-observation synthesis, NASA's render, and any later processing.

nodes.label: Never Fake a Measurement or a Control
nodes.norm_label: never fake a measurement or a control
nodes.rationale: Unavailable systems are labeled, not simulated; a disabled control must show the reason it cannot be used.

nodes.label: Provenance Is Part of the Interface
nodes.norm_label: provenance is part of the interface
nodes.rationale: The visitor can always tell what is measured, modeled, rendered, or derived; original scientific data, NASA's rendering, and derived/normalized data are named as different things.

nodes.label: Science Before Spectacle
nodes.rationale: A beautiful interface that blurs provenance is a failure.

nodes.label: Build the Smallest Trustworthy System That Can Grow
nodes.norm_label: build the smallest trustworthy system that can grow

nodes.label: Statement: NASA's Visualization Is a Rendering, Not a Measurement
nodes.norm_label: statement: nasa's visualization is a rendering, not a measurement

nodes.label: CSS Design Tokens (globals.css)
nodes.rationale: All visual decisions live as CSS custom properties plus component classes; Tailwind is present but utility classes are avoided for the core instrument layout because the brief required a precise, non-generic composition.

nodes.label: Instrument Cyan (#42c7d9)
nodes.rationale: Reserved for meaning and interaction (links, focus, available status, loading progress) and never used as a background wash.

nodes.label: Tagline: Listen to What You Cannot See
nodes.norm_label: tagline: listen to what you cannot see

nodes.label: Explore Surface Direction Contract
nodes.rationale: The brief pins the visual world, so no concept roll was run; the nearest rut (dark neon dashboard) is explicitly refused. The plate must be the largest object on screen and every disabled control must explain its missing subsystem.

nodes.label: Accessibility Implementation
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 must already be keyboard-operable, screen-reader legible, reduced-motion aware, and free of color-only status; disabled controls expose their reason through visible text and aria-describedby. No formal WCAG audit is claimed.

nodes.label: Brand Commitments (Earth's Pulse, NASA attribution)
nodes.rationale: The brief pins the visual world (near-black navy ground, restrained cyan accents, Inter for reading, mono for measurements, no glassmorphism, no neon, no emoji). NASA attribution is mandatory and must distinguish NASA's visualization from this independent, non-endorsed challenge project.

nodes.label: The Calibrated Plate (Design North Star)
nodes.rationale: The system borrows composure from research charts and observatory consoles so the ocean image can carry the page while provenance can interrupt the mood without feeling bolted on. It explicitly refuses the dark neon dashboard, glass panels, gradient spectacle, hero metrics, and fake charts that would make an unavailable scientific system look finished.

nodes.label: The Hairline Rule
nodes.rationale: Structure is drawn with 1px rules and tonal shifts rather than rounded cards, glass, or panel shadows, which keeps the plate the only elevated object.

nodes.label: The Measurement Mono Rule
nodes.rationale: IBM Plex Mono is reserved for things that were looked up, measured, or timed (identifiers, coordinates, timestamps, units, machine status), which keeps prose in Inter and prevents the mono face from becoming decorative.

nodes.label: The One Signal Rule
nodes.rationale: Cyan means available or active, amber means blocked or incomplete, neutral grey means pending; these hues are never decoration. Availability must never be communicated by color alone.

nodes.label: The Single Lift Rule
nodes.rationale: Depth is tonal by default; only the visualization plate casts a shadow so it reads as mounted above the page without turning panels into floating cards.

nodes.label: Audio Is an Equal Access Path
nodes.norm_label: audio is an equal access path
nodes.rationale: Sonification is an interpretation of data, not an atmosphere; the product exists because visual-only science excludes people, so future audio must ship with equivalent textual state and never sound alone.

nodes.label: Deep Navy + Cyan Accent Palette
nodes.rationale: Background #080d16 with a #42c7d9 stroke and low-opacity #9bc8d8 grid lines: the dark plate keeps the favicon visible against light and dark browser chrome, and the cyan accent is the same signal color used in the data visualization.

nodes.label: Single-Meridian Globe Grid Motif
nodes.rationale: One circle plus one full-height ellipse (rx 5.6, ry 12.5, no equator line) reads as a globe at 16px while staying under ~6 SVG elements, keeping the favicon legible in a browser tab.

nodes.label: Jagged Waveform Mark (Pulse Line)
nodes.rationale: The polyline is an ECG-like spike sequence with one dominant peak, encoding the product name 'Earth's Pulse' as a data signal across the globe rather than as lettering, which would be unreadable at favicon size.

nodes.label: Baked-In Plate Layers Limitation (no separate temperature/current layers)
nodes.norm_label: baked-in plate layers limitation (no separate temperature/current layers)

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus training data, so the relevant guide under node_modules/next/dist/docs must be read before writing code. The block is regenerated by `next dev`, so committing it keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: Product Stack (Next.js App Router, React, TS strict, Tailwind)
nodes.norm_label: product stack (next.js app router, react, ts strict, tailwind)
nodes.rationale: Scientific preprocessing will be Python/NumPy/xarray later, so the TypeScript data model stays UI-independent and serializable; Canvas/SVG only when a visual overlay needs it, with no Three.js or 3D globe in Stage 1.

nodes.label: ECCO2 - MITgcm Model
nodes.rationale: ECCO2 is a data-assimilating model output, not an observation - the page states 'data-assimilating model not direct measurement'. This is the single most load-bearing honesty claim on the page.

nodes.label: Three Layers of Evidence
nodes.rationale: Design principle: separate what NASA produced (numerical field), what NASA rendered (image), and what this project derives (processed data), so a viewer can never mistake a pretty frame for a measurement. Layer 1 is explicitly not certified; only the rendered image carries 'certified'.

nodes.label: Data Sources and Provenance Page (Mobile)
nodes.rationale: Full-height mobile reference screenshot of the provenance page captured at 380x4602, used as the long-scroll baseline for the review pass. The page exists to answer 'what is rendered, what is simulated, and what is not' before any audio claim is made.

nodes.label: Explore Page - Desktop Rendered Plate (Stage 01)
nodes.rationale: Primary desktop composition: hero title + three-column metadata row, large plate viewer left, two stacked reference panels right (Source Record, Signal Path), transport bar below, and a persistent NOT LIVE footer. Purpose is a museum-label layout - the artifact dominates, provenance annotates it.

nodes.label: Plate 01 / Global Viewer
nodes.rationale: 2048x1024 plate shown inside a bordered frame with corner registration ticks and a caption strip naming the source (NASA SVS / Greg Shirah) and the frame timestamp. Corners + caption make the image read as a scientific plate rather than a hero graphic.

nodes.label: Sonification Transport (Offline)
nodes.rationale: Disabled transport bar with OFFLINE chip, 'Audio engine not implemented. Stage 02 will map verified ECCO2 fields to Web Audio; playback stays disabled until then.', a NOT SYNCHRONIZED timeline, speed control (0.5x/1x/2x) and two layer toggles greyed out. Ships the final control surface in a disabled state so the affordance is not invented later.

nodes.label: Source Record Panel
nodes.rationale: Key/value ledger (Visualization, Record SVS 3912, Publisher, Model, Period, Credit, Plate frame, Plate file) with a VERIFIED status dot, an 'Open NASA record' external link, and a 'Validated 14 Nov 2026' stamp. Duplicates provenance inline so the viewer never has to leave the plate to check it.

nodes.label: Explore Page - Rendered Plate Unavailable (Error State)
nodes.norm_label: explore page - rendered plate unavailable (error state)
nodes.rationale: Failure state keeps the entire page intact - hero, metadata, both right-hand panels and transport all remain - and only the plate frame degrades. Message: 'Rendered plate unavailable. The local NASA still could not be loaded. The source record is still available.' with an alt-text description of the missing image rendered in place.

nodes.label: Cache Disabled Dev Banner
nodes.rationale: Floating amber 'N Cache disabled x' toast bottom-left, overlapping the logo and the transport's left edge. Development-only instrumentation that also appears in the loading capture, which is why both screenshots show it.

nodes.label: Open NASA SVS 3912 Recovery Link
nodes.rationale: The error state's only call to action points outward to the authoritative source rather than to a retry, so the provenance guarantee survives the image being gone.

nodes.label: Explore Page - Loading Rendered Plate (Loading State)
nodes.norm_label: explore page - loading rendered plate (loading state)
nodes.rationale: Loading state shows 'NASA SVS / 3912' eyebrow, 'Loading rendered plate' label and an indeterminate thin progress bar inside the otherwise empty bordered plate frame. Layout is identical to the loaded and error states, so no reflow occurs between the three.

nodes.label: Access Limitations and Next Step
nodes.rationale: Explains that numerical-field access is not free via API, requires training/specialist support, and needs an Earthdata login or API credentials - plus a size caveat (the dataset is far larger than a single browser session, so it will be subset/chunked). This is the stated blocker for Stage 02.

nodes.label: Derived / Processed Data (NASA Asset, Derived)
nodes.rationale: Reserved layer for sonified output and any rescaling the project itself performs. Declared up front so future audio/derived artifacts are never retrofitted into the 'raw' layers.

nodes.label: What the Image Can and Cannot Show
nodes.norm_label: what the image can and cannot show
nodes.rationale: Two-column honest-limits table. CAN SHOW: spatial pattern of modelled surface current flow, season and basin-scale currents, where warm currents and eddies appear, one depiction near 2007-2008. CANNOT SHOW: singular temperature values, numerical velocity, unlabelled uncertainty, a live ocean, and precise place-level conditions (only ocean-basin scale).

nodes.label: Licensing and Attribution
nodes.rationale: NASA imagery is public domain but NASA does not endorse the project; ECCO2 products carry a citation condition and the derived output inherits it. Footer restates: 'Independent project. Not an official NASA product.'

nodes.label: Numerical Field (NASA Asset, Not Certified)
nodes.rationale: ECCO2 surface current (u, v) and sea surface temperature; 0.25 deg, daily mean 26 Mar 2007 - 03 Mar 2008 as NetCDF/Granule inputs. Declared 'not certified' here because the certification line applies to the visualization, not the field.

nodes.label: Rendered Visualization (NASA Asset, Certified)
nodes.rationale: One frame of NASA SVS 3912, 2048x1024 JPEG, published 7 May 2008, credited Greg Shirah / NASA GSFC. Certified because NASA's published record is the authoritative artifact - the project does not re-render or re-derive it.

nodes.label: Source Record Ledger (Every Claim Traced)
nodes.rationale: Rule stated on-page: 'every row below was checked against its publisher' and 'The last two rows are explicitly not part of this build.' Rows are grouped NASA SVS (3912, high-res, EECO2 derived still), ECCO2 (product overview, numerical fields), EECO2 PODAAC, plus NASA/ECCO2 licensing and FAS citation links.

nodes.label: NOT LIVE Disclaimer (Historical Model Output)
nodes.rationale: Repeated at four altitudes - nav badge 'STAGE 01 / VISUAL ONLY', hero bullet 'HISTORICAL MODEL OUTPUT - 26 MAR 2007 - 03 MAR 2008 - NOT LIVE', plate header 'RENDERED VISUALIZATION - NOT LIVE', and the page footer 'NOTHING ON THIS SCREEN IS A LIVE OCEAN OBSERVATION.' Repetition is deliberate: any single occurrence could be scrolled past.

nodes.label: Read the Plate as a Rendering (Callout)
nodes.norm_label: read the plate as a rendering (callout)
nodes.rationale: Inline anti-misreading callout: 'Pixel colors are not measurements. The image is NASA's rendered visualization; numerical ECCO2 fields are not connected in this stage.' with a link to data provenance. Placed at the moment of looking, not buried in an About page.

nodes.label: Signal Path Panel (04 Stages)
nodes.rationale: Exposes the four-stage sonification pipeline (01 Numerical field, 02 Normalize, 03 Map, 04 Audio graph) with per-stage status chips - NOT CONNECTED, PENDING, PENDING, NOT IMPLEMENTED - and the closing note 'The path stops at the field boundary. No scientific value reaches the audio layer in this stage.' Showing the unfinished pipeline is the honesty mechanism; it converts an absence of audio into visible, legible state.

nodes.label: Plate Frame Skeleton (Stable Geometry)
nodes.rationale: The frame, corner ticks, header strip and caption strip are rendered before the image resolves, reserving exact geometry. This is what makes loaded/loading/error visually interchangeable apart from the interior.

nodes.label: Liveness Honesty Principle — Status Labels Everywhere Instead of Implied Capability
nodes.norm_label: liveness honesty principle — status labels everywhere instead of implied capability
nodes.rationale: Recurring design decision across the Explore view: every affordance carries its own truthful status (NOT LIVE, OFFLINE, NOT CONNECTED, PENDING, NOT IMPLEMENTED, VERIFIED) so the product can ship an unfinished sonification stage without overstating what is measured, rendered, or audible.

nodes.label: Read the Plate as a Rendering — Callout ('Pixel colors are not measurements')
nodes.norm_label: read the plate as a rendering — callout ('pixel colors are not measurements')
nodes.rationale: Design intent: separate the scientific artifact (numerical ECCO2 fields, not connected at this stage) from the raster that ships (a rendered visualization), preventing the expressive color ramp from being read as measured data. The callout is a deliberate honesty device, not decoration.
